title: Session-budgeted retries and interruptible stream ergonomics for Python/TS/Go SDKs
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Cross-language SDKs currently expose disparate retry primitives (per-call backoffs, ad-hoc idempotency handling) and awkward streaming ergonomics (hard to resume or abort with predictable cost control). Production apps need predictable unit economics: retries should be bounded at the session level (per logical user/session) and streams should support cheap, safe interruption and resumability without surprising duplicate side effects.

Proposal: Implement a session-budgeted retry model + interruptible/resumable stream ergonomics across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. Key pieces: 1) Session object that scopes a retry budget (token-bucket) used by sync calls, async calls, and streaming resumptions. 2) Cross-SDK default backoff profiles (fast-fail for non-idempotent ops, conservative exponential for idempotent ops) with jitter and cost-aware caps. 3) Idempotency key semantics: when SDK auto-generates keys, collision window, rotation, and guidance for customers. 4) Streaming ergonomics: explicit resume tokens, on_resume hooks, shallow checkpoints for chunked responses (KV offsets) and a lightweight abort-with-grace to drain resources. 5) Telemetry: per-session metrics (retry_attempts, budget_remaining, resume_count, resume_success_rate) and standard tags to correlate to requests.

Why session-budgeted? Many of our customers open long-lived sessions (chat UX, interactive apps) where naive per-request retries lead to unbounded costs during failure storms or retries triggered by many parallel components. A session budget places a predictable upper bound and enables smarter allocation (e.g., reserve tokens for streaming resume vs background retries).

Cross-language goals: identical logical semantics and defaults across Python/TS/Go while keeping idiomatic APIs for each language.

Implementation notes: The Session should be cheap to create and copy (immutable config + shared atomic counters for budget). SDKs will expose a default global Session for backwards compatibility. Streaming layer will exchange resume tokens in the response metadata (server-side change coordinated with runtime teams) but provide a client-side emulation path where the SDK stitches partial responses locally and uses sequence offsets as resume checkpoints.
acceptance_criteria:
1) SDKs expose Session(config) with fields: retry_budget, budget_window_seconds, idempotency_policy (auto|explicit|none), backoff_profile (fast|standard|conservative).
2) Default profiles across Python/TS/Go match the spec and are documented.
3) Streaming API surfaces: session.start_stream(...), stream.on_resume(callback), stream.resume(resume_token) and stream.abort(graceful=true).
4) Idempotency keys: SDK auto-generates for listed operations and emits warning logs when auto-generation is used for non-idempotent endpoints.
5) Telemetry emitted: metric names retry.session_attempts, retry.session_budget_used, stream.resume_attempts, stream.resume_success with tags {language, profile, endpoint}.
6) Integration tests simulate failure storms and validate budget bounds and correct resume behavior.
7) Example snippets added to SDK READMEs for Python/TS/Go.
8) Cross-language compliance tests pass (shared test harness).
design_notes:
- Budget model: token bucket with burst equal to 20% of window capacity. Default window = 300s, default budget = 50 tokens (tunable). Each retry attempt consumes 1 token; streaming resume consumes 2 tokens by default.
- Backoff profiles: fast = initial 100ms, multiplier 1.6, cap 2s; standard = 250ms, multiplier 2, cap 8s; conservative = 500ms, multiplier 2.5, cap 30s. All profiles use full jitter.
- Idempotency semantics: if request declares operation as non-idempotent, SDK will not retry without explicit user-provided idempotency key. For operations considered idempotent by our catalog, SDK may auto-generate keys using session_id + monotonic counter + random suffix and will include idempotency-key expiration header (X-Idemp-Window: 300s).
- Streaming resume: server will return resume_token metadata when response is partially complete. SDK will persist minimal resume state (offsets and last meta) and attempt resume using session credentials and resume_token. If resume fails due to budget exhaustion, SDK surfaces a distinct error type RetryBudgetExceeded.
- Telemetry: expose counters and histograms via existing SDK telemetry bridges (OpenTelemetry metrics tags recommended).
- Opt-out: customers can opt out of session-budgeted retry by passing idempotency_policy=none or setting retry_budget=0.
examples:
Go:
sess := redwood.NewSession(redwood.SessionOptions{RetryBudget:30, BudgetWindowSeconds:600, BackoffProfile:"conservative"})
cli := redwood.NewClient(redwood.ClientOptions{Session: sess})

stream, err := cli.StartStream(ctx, "document")
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
stream.OnResume(func(token string){ log.Printf("resumed %s", token) })
for chunk := range stream.Chan() { log.Println(chunk.Text) }
